title: ScanProfile
description: The only input that may be sent to the server. It describes what the product is, never what its code says: source fragments, file paths and identifiers must never appear here. A PROFILE IS VALIDATED AGAINST THIS SCHEMA AT RUNTIME, AT BOTH LOAD SITES, FROM 2026-09-02. `product/packages/cli/src/profile.ts` `loadScanProfile` parses the file, compiles this schema with Ajv and checks the profile against it, and both `--profile` consumers - `product/packages/cli/src/scan.ts` and `product/packages/cli/src/reconcile.ts` - go through that one step instead of casting a parsed file. WHAT A VIOLATION DOES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: every violation is printed before anything else the command says, naming the JSON path, what this schema wanted, what was found and how the run treated it, AND THE RUN CONTINUES. Each violating FIELD is treated as unanswered - the field is replaced with `null`, which the engine's precondition evaluator documents as "I did not answer" and never as "no" - so the rules and gate limbs that name it still run and carry the open question. FIELD, NOT NODE: where the violation sits inside an array the validator names the ELEMENT, and what is replaced is the array that contains it, because an array carrying a member this schema rejects is not a usable answer and `[null]` is still an array that a `contains` or a length test reads as one. (Corrected 2026-09-02, the day it was written: the first draft nulled the element, and the independent check measured `distribution_regions: ["europe"]` coming back as an answer of no.) Only a file that is not an object of answers at all is discarded whole, and a discarded profile is `null`, the state in which every rule runs. NOTHING IS EVER REFUSED AND NOTHING IS EVER NARROWED: an unanswered precondition suppresses nothing, so the downgrade can only add rules to a run, and a scan the tool declined to perform would be the largest available form of the failure this product exists to prevent. Where the validator itself cannot be loaded the profile is used as written and the run says so in the block and in `profile_validation.ran: false` with its reason, which is a disclosure and is never read as a pass. The record of every check is `profile_validation` on `Findings` and on `ReconcileInput`, and `violations[].found` carries the rejected value verbatim, so what the file held survives beside what the run read. THAT CHECK RETURNED FAIL ON ITS FIRST PASS - three moderate defects, none of them a narrowing: an array-element downgrade that left the field readable as an answer, a `declared_artifacts` downgrade that lost its own reason, and two descriptions of the new record that its code contradicted. All six of its findings are repaired in the same change this sentence sits in. This sentence names the check; it is not a clearance. THE PASSAGE THIS REPLACES IS KEPT AS THE RECORD, WORD FOR WORD, BECAUSE IT WAS TRUE AND MEASURED WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND IT IS WHAT MADE THIS CHANGE ASKABLE: "NOTHING VALIDATES A PROFILE AGAINST THIS SCHEMA AT RUNTIME, measured 2026-08-05. No Ajv instance in this repository compiles this file; `product/packages/cli/src/scan.ts` and `product/packages/cli/src/reconcile.ts` both cast a parsed `--profile` to `ScanProfile` without validating it; `ajv` is not a dependency of the CLI package, so it is unavailable there rather than merely unused; and none of the eleven sub-scripts of `npm run gates` reads this file. Every constraint written here is therefore a SPECIFICATION that whatever produces a profile is expected to honour, and not a check that rejects a profile which does not - and that is EVERY constraint, not the four an earlier version of this sentence named: measured on 2026-08-05, the constraint keywords in this file are `additionalProperties`, `type`, `pattern`, `enum`, `const`, `required`, `items`, `minItems` and `maxLength`, nine of them, and `maxLength` is the one `supply.licence.spdx_id` leans on. Read it as the contract, never as the enforcement. Turning validation on is a behaviour change and needs its own approval and its own independent check; it is deliberately not made here." TWO OF ITS SENTENCES ARE ALMOST STILL TRUE AND ARE NOT SUPERSEDED, WITH ONE CORRECTION TO THE FIRST. The nine constraint keywords the 2026-08-05 census enumerates are all still used - but they are not all of them: measured over this whole file on 2026-09-02, the keywords are `additionalProperties`, `allOf`, `const`, `contains`, `enum`, `items`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `not`, `pattern`, `required` and `type`, TWELVE, the extra three being the `not`/`allOf`/`contains` combination on `distribution_regions` that keeps "unknown" from sitting beside a country. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-07, AND THE CENSUS IS NOW THIRTEEN: `format` joined them with `business.size.as_of`, which is the house convention for a date field - `rule.schema.json` and `checklist.schema.json` both use `format: "date"`. It is asserted rather than ignored, because both Ajv instances that compile this file - `tools/build-bundle.mjs` and `product/packages/cli/src/schema-validate.ts` - construct `Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: false })` and then call `addFormats`, read in both files on 2026-09-07. That census was already short at HEAD and this correction is the first thing to say so; `product/packages/cli/src/profile.ts` carries a branch written for `not` precisely because this file uses it. The second sentence stands unchanged: every constraint here is still a SPECIFICATION of what a profile producer is expected to honour - what changed is that failing to honour one is now noticed and said out loud, not that it is refused. SOME OPTIONAL FIELDS NARROW WHO IS ASKING, which is a different concern from the prohibition above and is not covered by it: a truthful answer to an optional field can narrow the population of people who could have sent this profile even though it carries no source fragment, no file path and nothing read from the tree. `supply.licence.spdx_id` is the field that states its own residual in its own description and is optional for that reason. IT IS NOT THE ONLY FIELD WITH THE PROPERTY AND THIS SENTENCE NO LONGER SAYS IT IS. CORRECTED 2026-08-05: it read "Every field with that property states its own residual in its own description and is optional for that reason; `supply.licence.spdx_id` is the one that has it today", which is the unscoped quantifier that `supply.licence.spdx_id`'s own `$comment` had already withdrawn and replaced with "the one field in `supply` that can narrow". Measured on 2026-08-05, four other optional fields take arbitrary strings with neither an `enum` nor a `pattern` on them - `stacks[]`, `features.llm.providers[]`, `features.payments.provider` and `features.analytics_ads[]` - and none of those four says what a truthful answer to it narrows, `stacks` coming closest with "Used to narrow detectors, not to identify the codebase", which is about what the field is used for. `supply.licence.spdx_id`'s own description names `platform`, `stacks` and `distribution_regions` as fields a single-vendor identifier combines with. Whether the other four should state a residual is a granularity decision and the owner's; it is recorded here rather than taken.

x-declaration-questions.source: THE ONE SOURCE OF THE DECLARATION QUESTIONS. Each field the program may ask carries an x-question object; the program (product/packages/cli/src/declaration.ts) reads them from this file, asks only those a candidate of the run turns on - through its rule's scope (jurisdiction, applicability_preconditions) or through a context question its seat is asked that names the field by its path - and appends the run's figures to the text. A field with per "part" is asked in parts (AskUserQuestion carries at most four choices, Not answering one of them), its value the first part answered with a value. A question's version is the sha256 of its x-question object, so a changed text or choice is asked again; the program's own keys (`kind`, `when`, `settles` and each option's `settles_as`), which the person never reads, are left out of it, so a change to how the program uses an answer asks nothing again. Every x-question carries a `kind` (`scope`, `condition`, `feature`, `order`), and the options of a scope or condition question carry `settles_as` (`out_of_scope`, `met`, `stands`, `maker`): what an answer does is data here, and no rule declares it. Ajv compiles this file with strict: false, so neither keyword changes validation.

ASKED OF THE PERSON RUNNING THE SCAN, NEVER INFERRED FROM CODE - a headcount, a turnover and a balance sheet total are not in a repository at all, and nothing in a tree corroborates or contradicts them. The block holds ONE question today, `size`, which is the enterprise-size question four EU instruments put to a reader before any duty of theirs is reached. AN ANSWER HERE LABELS WHAT A RULE REPORTS AND NEVER STOPS A RULE FROM READING: no answer in this block removes a rule from a scan, shortens a walk or suppresses a candidate, and `unknown` is a first-class answer rather than a missing one. Every field is optional and a profile that omits the whole block is valid; an absent answer must never be read as an answer in either direction. Nothing here is sent anywhere the rest of this profile is not, and the prohibition at the root of this schema applies unchanged: no source fragment, no file path and no identifier read from the tree may appear in any field of this block.

Its second subparagraph carries the tail that makes `as_of` load-bearing: the Section also does not apply to providers "that previously qualified for the status of a micro or small enterprise as defined in Recommendation 2003/361/EC during the 12 months following their loss of that status pursuant to Article 4(2) thereof, except when they are very large online platforms in accordance with Article 33". THE EUROPEAN ACCESSIBILITY ACT DEFINES THE WORD ITSELF AND DOES NOT POINT AT THE RECOMMENDATION, so a reader must not assume the two definitions are the same text. Directive (EU) 2019/882, Art. 3(23), fetched 2026-09-07: "'microenterprise' means an enterprise which employs fewer than 10 persons and which has an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2 million or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million"; Art. 4(5): "Microenterprises providing services shall be exempt from complying with the accessibility requirements referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article and any obligations relating to the compliance with those requirements." THE TWO MICRO SETS COINCIDE, AND THE COMPARISON IS SHOWN RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Both take the same staff limb, "employs fewer than 10 persons", word for word. Both cap turnover and balance sheet at EUR 2 million. The words for the financial limb differ - the EAA writes "an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2 million or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million", the Recommendation's Art. 2(3) "whose annual turnover and/or annual balance sheet total does not exceed EUR 2 million" - and on the ordinary reading of "and/or" as "either or both" the two describe the same set, so `size.class` answered `micro` answers the EAA gate as well. That reading is stated rather than hidden, and this block settles nothing for a case where only one of the two measures is known. ONE ASYMMETRY POINTS THE OTHER WAY AND IS RECORDED BEFORE IT BITES: EAA Art. 3(24) defines SMEs as enterprises "which employ fewer than 250 persons and which have an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million, or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 43 million, but excludes microenterprises" - the opposite of the Recommendation's cumulative structure, in which a microenterprise is within the SME category. So `class` is NOT directly reusable for an EAA row that turns on "SME", and the smallest-category instruction at `class` is what keeps that repairable. THAT SAME EXPECTATIONS FILE RECORDS A SECOND ASK-FACT THAT STILL HAS NO FIELD - whether what is supplied is a covered consumer service, EAA Art. 2(2) read with the Art. 3(30) e-commerce definition - which none of A2's five fields carries and which this unit does not build. It remains owed to the A format bundle. ADDING THE QUESTION IS NOT ADDING A ROW: nothing in this change makes a rule fire, stop firing or report differently. THE ROOT DESCRIPTION'S KEYWORD CENSUS IS ONE SHORT FROM 2026-09-07 AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION. That census, taken 2026-09-02, lists twelve constraint keywords in this file; `size.as_of` uses `format`, which is the THIRTEENTH, and it is the house convention for a date field (`rule.schema.json` and `checklist.schema.json` both use `format: "date"`). Both Ajv instances that compile this schema - `tools/build-bundle.mjs` and `product/packages/cli/src/schema-validate.ts` - construct `Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: false })` and call `addFormats`, verified by reading both files on 2026-09-07, so the keyword is asserted rather than ignored. `additionalProperties: false` is still set at every object level in this file: measured 2026-09-07 at 12 occurrences, against the 10 the `supply` block measured on 2026-08-05, the two new ones being this object and `size`. ONE OTHER MEASURED SENTENCE IN THIS FILE IS OVERTAKEN BY `size.basis_note` AND IS DELIBERATELY LEFT STANDING. The root description and `supply.licence.spdx_id`'s `$comment` each record, dated 2026-08-05, that four fields elsewhere in this profile take arbitrary strings with neither an `enum` nor a `pattern` on them - `stacks[]`, `features.llm.providers[]`, `features.payments.provider` and `features.analytics_ads[]`. Both sentences are explicitly dated and remain true of the day they were measured; `basis_note` makes it FIVE as of 2026-09-07, and that count is stated at `basis_note` itself and in the TypeScript mirror, whose sentence was present-tense and was corrected.

size.description: How big is the enterprise that ships this product? Answered by the person running the scan, from their own accounts, and never inferred from code. Four EU instruments ask this before any duty of theirs is reached, and each of them defines the categories by pointing at Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, which is where every threshold below comes from. ANSWER THE FIRST FIELD IF YOU ANSWER NOTHING ELSE: `class` is the one every reader wants, and the three band fields, the linked-enterprises answer, the date and the note exist so that a reader can see what the class rests on. `unknown` IS A REAL ANSWER HERE and it is the honest one where the figures have not been worked out. It is not read as small and not read as large: a size-gated row is reported as an open question against the enterprise rather than as one that does or does not reach it.
size.$comment: THE THRESHOLDS ARE QUOTED FROM THE SOURCE RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED FROM MEMORY. Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, Annex, Article 2, "Staff headcount and financial ceilings determining enterprise categories", retrieved 2026-09-07. Art. 2(1): "The category of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) is made up of enterprises which employ fewer than 250 persons and which have an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million, and/or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 43 million." Art. 2(2): "Within the SME category, a small enterprise is defined as an enterprise which employs fewer than 50 persons and whose annual turnover and/or annual balance sheet total does not exceed EUR 10 million." Art. 2(3): "Within the SME category, a microenterprise is defined as an enterprise which employs fewer than 10 persons and whose annual turnover and/or annual balance sheet total does not exceed EUR 2 million." Art. 1 fixes what an enterprise is: "An enterprise is considered to be any entity engaged in an economic activity, irrespective of its legal form. This includes, in particular, self-employed persons and family businesses engaged in craft or other activities, and partnerships or associations regularly engaged in an economic activity." So a single-person project sold commercially is an enterprise for this purpose and answers `micro` rather than omitting the block. ROUTE NOTE, MEASURED 2026-09-07. The Publications Office cellar route for this Recommendation does not serve a document: `https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32003H0361` with `Accept: application/xhtml+xml` answered HTTP 404 with the body "cellar identifier cellar:6ca8d655-126b-4a42-ada4-e9058fa45155 does not hold a content datastream of the requested type". The EUR-Lex HTML route https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32003H0361 answered HTTP 200 on the same day and is the route every quotation in this block was read from, the four referring provisions included. NO BYTE COUNT IS OFFERED AS PROVENANCE FOR ANY OF THEM, DELIBERATELY: EUR-Lex serves this HTML dynamically, so a byte figure would be a number the next reader cannot reproduce. The measurements behind that sentence are observations about the route and are not provenance for any quotation: two fetches of the same document minutes apart on 2026-09-07 differed in length (this Recommendation 26,512 then 26,513 bytes; Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 836,649 then 840,294), and an independent check's own fetches the same day returned different figures again (25,994 and 839,775). Reworded 2026-09-07: the sentence said no byte count was cited and then cited four. WHY BANDS AND NOT NUMBERS. Every provision that reads this asks which side of a threshold the enterprise is on and none of them asks for the figure, so the figure is not collected: a headcount and a turnover are the two data points that identify a small company most sharply, and this profile is the one thing that may leave the user's machine. The bands are drawn AT the Recommendation's own ceilings, so no band straddles a threshold and no arithmetic is needed to read one. Each band names the LOWEST ceiling the figure does not exceed, which makes the values disjoint and ordered: an enterprise with a turnover of EUR 1 million answers `le_2m`, not `le_10m`. WHY `class` IS DECLARED AND NOT COMPUTED FROM THE BANDS. It cannot be computed from them. Annex Art. 3 makes the category turn on relationships this profile does not carry - autonomous, partner and linked enterprises - and Art. 6(2) then requires the partner enterprise's data to be added "proportional to the percentage interest in the capital or voting rights (whichever is greater)" and "100 % of the data of any enterprise, which is linked directly or indirectly to the enterprise in question, where the data were not already included through consolidation in the accounts" - the closing condition was restored 2026-09-07, the quotation having stopped one clause short and stated the rule slightly more absolutely than the text does. Proportional aggregation over another enterprise's accounts cannot be done from four band labels. THE RECOMMENDATION ITSELF CONTEMPLATES THE DECLARATION, which is why this is a declared field at all - Art. 3(5): "Enterprises may make a declaration of status as an autonomous enterprise, partner enterprise or linked enterprise, including the data regarding the ceilings set out in Article 2." WHY `as_of` AND WHY IT IS NOT DECORATION. Annex Art. 4(1): "The data to apply to the headcount of staff and the financial amounts are those relating to the latest approved accounting period and calculated on an annual basis. They are taken into account from the date of closure of the accounts." Art. 4(2) then makes the status sticky: "Where, at the date of closure of the accounts, an enterprise finds that, on an annual basis, it has exceeded or fallen below the headcount or financial ceilings stated in Article 2, this will not result in the loss or acquisition of the status of medium-sized, small or microenterprise unless those ceilings are exceeded over two consecutive accounting periods." A single year over a ceiling is therefore not a change of class, and DSA Art. 19(1)'s second subparagraph runs a further 12 months from a loss of status "pursuant to Article 4(2) thereof" - so the date the figures belong to is part of the answer and not metadata about it. Art. 4(3) covers a newly established enterprise whose accounts are not yet approved: "the data to apply is to be derived from a bona fide estimate made in the course of the financial year", which is an answer this block accepts like any other, with `basis_note` the place to say it is an estimate. WHAT THIS BLOCK DOES NOT ASK. Headcount is defined in annual work units by Annex Art. 5, which counts employees, subordinated persons deemed employees under national law, owner-managers and partners engaging in a regular activity, and excludes apprentices and students on training contracts and the duration of maternity or parental leave. This block asks for the band and not for the working, and Art. 5 is quoted at `staff_headcount_band` so that a person answering it counts the same population the provisions do.

parts.question: Under the EU's own definition, Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC: is the company within the SME category - fewer than 250 people, and an annual turnover up to EUR 50M or a balance sheet total up to EUR 43M?

options.label: SME
options.description: Within the SME category: the next question says which size

options.label: Larger
options.description: Outside the SME category

parts.question: If the company is within the SME category, which size is it? Answer with the smallest that fits.

options.label: Micro
options.description: Fewer than 10 people, and turnover or balance sheet up to EUR 2M

options.label: Small
options.description: Fewer than 50 people, and turnover or balance sheet up to EUR 10M

options.label: Medium
options.description: Within the SME category, neither micro nor small

class.description: Which category is the enterprise in, under Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC? Your own classification, and the four instruments that read it all define the categories by pointing at that Recommendation. `micro` - fewer than 10 persons and annual turnover and/or annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million. `small` - fewer than 50 persons and annual turnover and/or annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 10 million. `medium` - fewer than 250 persons and annual turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million, and/or annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 43 million. `large` - none of the three. THE RECOMMENDATION DEFINES NO STANDALONE "medium-sized enterprise" EITHER: Art. 2(1) draws the whole SME category and Arts. 2(2) and 2(3) carve the two smaller ones out of it, so `medium` here means: inside Art. 2(1) and outside Arts. 2(2) and 2(3), which is what the smallest-category instruction below produces. (Added 2026-09-07: this was said for `large` and not for `medium`.) AND THE RECOMMENDATION DEFINES NO CATEGORY CALLED "large" AT ALL: the word here means only that the enterprise is outside the SME category as Art. 2(1) draws it, and nothing else follows from it. `unknown` - the figures have not been worked out, or the enterprise cannot say. Answer it rather than omitting the field where the question was put and could not be settled. AN `unknown` IS NEVER READ AS A SIZE: a size-gated row is reported as an open question, never as one that does not reach this enterprise. The categories are cumulative in the Recommendation's own structure - a microenterprise is also within the SME category - so answer with the SMALLEST category the enterprise is in, and let the reader widen it.
class.$comment: SMALLEST CATEGORY, NOT THE FIRST ONE THAT FITS. Art. 2(2) and 2(3) are both written "Within the SME category", so a microenterprise satisfies the small-enterprise ceilings too and a truthful answerer could pick either word. The instructed answer is the smallest, for one reason: the two exemptions written "micro or small" (DSA Art. 19(1), eIDAS 2 Art. 5f(2)) and the two written "small enterprises" alone (P2B Arts. 11(5), 12(7)) are not the same set of words, and only the smallest answer keeps that distinction visible to whoever reads it. WHY NO `is_sme` BOOLEAN. The same argument the owner settled for `supply` on 2026-08-05, in a different instrument: a single boolean collects an answer that settles none of the four tests. DSA Art. 19(1) and eIDAS 2 Art. 5f(2) turn on micro-or-small; P2B Arts. 11(5) and 12(7) on small; NIS2 Art. 2(1) on medium-or-above, which is the SME boundary read from the other side. A yes/no SME answer separates none of those three lines from each other. THE ANSWER IS A LABEL AND NOT A GATE. Under the ruling of 2026-08-27 an answer in a profile never removes a rule from a scan, so `micro` here cannot stop a DSA rule from reading a tree; it travels with what that rule reports. Nothing in this schema decides whether an exemption is reached - that is a reading of the instrument, made where the finding is adjudicated, with this answer in front of it.

staff_headcount_band.description: How many persons does the enterprise employ? Answer the band, not the number. The boundaries are the Recommendation's own: `lt_10` (fewer than 10, Art. 2(3)), `10_to_49` (fewer than 50 but not fewer than 10, Art. 2(2)), `50_to_249` (fewer than 250 but not fewer than 50, Art. 2(1)), `250_plus`, `unknown`. WHAT COUNTS AS A PERSON HERE IS DEFINED AND IS NOT A HEADCOUNT OF CONTRACTS. Annex Art. 5: "The headcount corresponds to the number of annual work units (AWU), i.e. the number of persons who worked full-time within the enterprise in question or on its behalf during the entire reference year under consideration. The work of persons who have not worked the full year, the work of those who have worked part-time, regardless of duration, and the work of seasonal workers are counted as fractions of AWU." The staff is "(a) employees; (b) persons working for the enterprise being subordinated to it and deemed to be employees under national law; (c) owner-managers; (d) partners engaging in a regular activity in the enterprise and benefiting from financial advantages from the enterprise", and "Apprentices or students engaged in vocational training with an apprenticeship or vocational training contract are not included as staff. The duration of maternity or parental leaves is not counted." Retrieved 2026-09-07.

annual_turnover_band_eur.description: What is the annual turnover? Answer the band, not the figure, and each band names the LOWEST ceiling the turnover does not exceed - EUR 1 million is `le_2m`, not `le_10m`. `le_2m` (Art. 2(3)'s microenterprise ceiling), `le_10m` (Art. 2(2)'s small-enterprise ceiling), `le_50m` (Art. 2(1)'s SME ceiling), `gt_50m`, `unknown`. TURNOVER AND BALANCE SHEET ARE ASKED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE RECOMMENDATION JOINS THEM WITH "and/or": Art. 2(1) reads "an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million, and/or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 43 million", so an enterprise over one ceiling and under the other is not thereby outside the category, and a single combined field could not express that. Annex Art. 4(1) says which year to use and what to exclude: the data are "those relating to the latest approved accounting period and calculated on an annual basis", and "The amount selected for the turnover is calculated excluding value added tax (VAT) and other indirect taxes." Retrieved 2026-09-07. Put that year in `as_of`.

balance_sheet_band_eur.description: What is the annual balance sheet total? Answer the band, not the figure, and each band names the LOWEST ceiling the total does not exceed. `le_2m` (Art. 2(3)), `le_10m` (Art. 2(2)), `le_43m` (Art. 2(1)), `gt_43m`, `unknown`. THE TOP CEILING IS EUR 43 MILLION AND NOT EUR 50 MILLION - the two limbs of Art. 2(1) carry different figures, "an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million, and/or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 43 million", which is why this field's bands are not the same as `annual_turnover_band_eur`'s. Retrieved 2026-09-07. Answer it for the same accounting period as the turnover, and put that period in `as_of`.

linked_enterprises_counted.description: Do the figures you gave INCLUDE the data of partner and linked enterprises? `true` if they do, `false` if they are this enterprise's own accounts alone. WHY THIS IS ASKED SEPARATELY. Annex Art. 3 divides enterprises into autonomous, partner and linked, and Art. 6 then says whose accounts go into the answer: for an autonomous enterprise "the data, including the number of staff, are determined exclusively on the basis of the accounts of that enterprise" (Art. 6(1)), while for an enterprise with partner or linked enterprises the data of each partner situated immediately upstream or downstream are added "proportional to the percentage interest in the capital or voting rights (whichever is greater)" and "100 % of the data of any enterprise, which is linked directly or indirectly to the enterprise in question, where the data were not already included through consolidation in the accounts" is added as well (Art. 6(2)). That closing condition is part of the quotation, and it is why a set of accounts already consolidated is not counted twice. An enterprise that answered from its own payroll alone has answered a different question from one that consolidated, and without this field a reader cannot tell which. `false` IS NOT A DEFECT AND IS NOT A CONFESSION. An autonomous enterprise - Art. 3(1), "any enterprise which is not classified as a partner enterprise within the meaning of paragraph 2 or as a linked enterprise within the meaning of paragraph 3" - has nothing to consolidate, and `false` is the accurate answer for it. It says the figures are unconsolidated, never that they should have been consolidated. OMIT THE FIELD RATHER THAN GUESSING. Nothing distinguishes a considered omission from a field nobody read, so an absent answer must not be read as an answer in either direction. Retrieved 2026-09-07.

as_of.description: Which accounting period do the figures above come from? An ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD), normally the date of closure of the accounts. IT IS PART OF THE ANSWER RATHER THAN METADATA ABOUT IT. Annex Art. 4(2) makes the class change only "unless those ceilings are exceeded over two consecutive accounting periods", so one year over a ceiling is not yet a change of class, and DSA Art. 19(1)'s second subparagraph runs a further 12 months from the loss of micro or small status "pursuant to Article 4(2) thereof". A class with no date cannot be read against either rule. For a newly established enterprise whose accounts are not yet approved, Art. 4(3) allows "a bona fide estimate made in the course of the financial year": give the date the estimate refers to and say it is an estimate in `basis_note`. Retrieved 2026-09-07.

basis_note.description: Anything a reader needs in order to read the answers above correctly, in free text: which accounts they came from, that a figure is an estimate under Annex Art. 4(3), which partner or linked enterprises were counted, or that the enterprise crossed a ceiling in one period only. Optional, and safely omitted. WHAT A TRUTHFUL ANSWER COSTS YOU, WHICH IS WHY IT IS OPTIONAL. This is free text, so it can narrow the population of people who could have sent this profile far more sharply than any band does - a named parent company, a named accountant, a funding round - and it is the only field in this block that can. Write nothing you would not put in front of the reader of a finding. THE ROOT PROHIBITION APPLIES HERE UNCHANGED AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY THE FIELD BEING FREE TEXT: no source fragment, no file path and no identifier read from the tree. Measured 2026-09-07: this is the FIFTH field in this profile taking arbitrary strings with neither an `enum` nor a `pattern`, after `stacks[]`, `features.llm.providers[]`, `features.payments.provider` and `features.analytics_ads[]`, and the first of the five to state what a truthful answer to it narrows. The two sentences in this file that count four are dated 2026-08-05 and are left standing as the measurements they were; the reason is recorded at `business`. The 2,000-character cap is a cap on a note and not a budget to fill.

supply.description: On what terms the product is supplied: whether it is free and open-source software, and whether it is monetised. ASKED OF THE PERSON RUNNING THE SCAN, NEVER INFERRED FROM CODE, on the same footing as `features.annex_iii_use` below. A LICENSE file, a sponsor badge, a pricing page and a paid-support link are evidence about these answers and are never the answers themselves. Answer `licence` and `monetisation` separately and answer both: two instruments turn on this fact and each of them turns on the COMBINATION of the two, so neither half settles anything on its own. NO ANSWER IN THIS BLOCK PUTS THE PRODUCT OUTSIDE EITHER INSTRUMENT. Under the CRA the free-and-open-source routes out are exemptions somebody claims, and no answer in this block claims one. Under the AI Act a system released under a free and open-source licence is nonetheless inside the Regulation where it is placed on the market or put into service as a high-risk AI system, or as a system falling under Article 5 or 50, and Article 2(12)'s own "unless" is what puts it there: Articles 5 and 50 reach such a system THROUGH that proviso and not independently of it. Nothing here is checked against anything: see the schema header. LEAVE A FIELD OUT WHERE YOU CANNOT ANSWER IT. ANSWER EACH FIELD FROM ITS OWN DESCRIPTION, including for the case for leaving the field out; where one of them turns out to be missing something you need, that description is what gets fixed rather than a note kept somewhere you were not sent. Nothing under `supply` is required, so an omission is always available and it claims nothing; it also cannot be told apart from a field nobody read, so an absent answer must never be read as a `false`.
supply.$comment: PROVENANCE. The monetisation answer has to be able to say HOW, because charging a price and accepting donations that do not exceed costs point in opposite directions under the same recital. THE TWO PROVISIONS. AI Act Art. 2(12) puts an AI system released under a free and open-source licence outside the Regulation unless it is placed on the market or put into service as high-risk or as a system falling under Article 5 or 50, and recital 103 takes that exception away again - on this block's reading of which of the AI Act's four free-and-open-source exceptions the carve-back reaches, recorded at `monetisation.by_anyone_including_third_parties` and at item (vii) below - where the component is "provided against a price or otherwise monetised, including through the provision of technical support or other services, including through a software platform, related to the AI component, or the use of personal data for reasons other than exclusively for improving the security, compatibility or interoperability of the software". The CRA does the same work through "in the course of a commercial activity" in Art. 3(22), elaborated by recitals 15, 16, 18 and 20. THAT ELEMENT IS NOT THE CRA'S ALONE and reading it as the CRA's distinguishing feature would be wrong: measured on 2026-08-05, the AI Act defines making available on the market in the same words at Art. 3(10) - "'making available on the market' means the supply of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge" - against CRA Art. 3(22)'s "'making available on the market' means the supply of a product with digital elements for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge". What differs between the two instruments is where each puts its free-and-open-source treatment, not the commercial-activity element. THE CRA DEFINES NO TERM "commercial activity" and a reader should not go looking for one: measured on the Official Journal text of 32024R2847 on 2026-08-05, Art. 3 runs to 51 defined terms and none of them is "commercial activity"; it is the recitals that characterise it. What Art. 3(48) defines is "free and open-source software", which is the other half of each CRA carve-out and is stated at `licence.free_and_open_source`. CORRECTION: an earlier version of that sentence put the two next to each other in a way that read as if Art. 3(48) defined the commercial-activity term (independent check, 2026-08-05). THREE OF THE THINGS THE TWO INSTRUMENTS EXPRESSLY TAKE OUT, AND THE LIST IS NOT CLOSED - a fourth of a different kind follows the three. CORRECTION: this sentence stated a closed count until the independent check of 2026-08-05 found the fourth. No field carries any of the three, because there is nothing for a person to declare. (1) OPEN REPOSITORIES, AND THE TWO INSTRUMENTS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS ABOUT THEM, so they are stated apart; running them together was this block's own recorded error, found by the independent check of 2026-08-05. AI Act recital 103: "The fact of making AI components available through open repositories should not, in itself, constitute a monetisation." That is a proposition about monetisation, and it is carried into the answer at `monetisation.by_anyone_including_third_parties`. CRA recital 20 is not about monetisation: "The sole act of hosting products with digital elements on open repositories, including through package managers or on collaboration platforms, does not in itself constitute the making available on the market of a product with digital elements", and its next sentence names whom it is addressed to - "Providers of such services should be considered to be distributors only if they make such software available on the market and hence supply it for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity". So the CRA's proposition is about the HOST and about making available on the market, which is a different test from whether the manufacturer monetises; `rules/gates/cra-scope.yaml`'s `hosting-on-an-open-repository-alone` limb cites recital 20 and is where that question lived when this was written. (2) HOW THE DEVELOPMENT WAS FINANCED. CRA recital 18: "The mere circumstances under which the product with digital elements has been developed, or how the development has been financed, should therefore not be taken into account when determining the commercial or non-commercial nature of that activity", and "the mere fact that an open-source software product with digital elements receives financial support from manufacturers or that manufacturers contribute to the development of such a product should not in itself determine that the activity is of commercial nature". A sponsorship page is an answer in neither direction. (3) RELEASE CADENCE. CRA recital 18 again: "the mere presence of regular releases should not in itself lead to the conclusion that a product with digital elements is supplied in the course of a commercial activity". A FOURTH EXPRESS CARVE-OUT, DIFFERENT IN KIND, WITH NO FIELD HERE FOR A DIFFERENT REASON. CRA recital 18 closes: "This Regulation does not apply to natural or legal persons who contribute with source code to products with digital elements qualifying as free and open-source software that are not under their responsibility." That one IS something a person can declare, so the reason no field carries it is not that there is nothing to declare. It is that it is a fact about WHO IS ASKING and not about how the product is supplied: it turns on the answerer's relationship to software somebody else is responsible for, whereas every field in this block takes THE PRODUCT BEING SCANNED as its subject. That is the only reading claimed, and it is narrower than the one the word "about" invites: it is not claimed that every field asks for a fact about the artefact, because two of the thirteen ask for a fact about a person or an organisation, which is correction (ii) below. `rules/gates/cra-scope.yaml` carried it as the limb `contributor-to-software-not-under-their-responsibility` when this was written. Whether this block should gain a field for it is a granularity decision and is deliberately not taken here. CORRECTIONS RECORDED ON 2026-08-05, FIFTH ROUND, EACH MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. (i) THE SCOPE-GATE SENTENCE. The description said "the scope gate stays open until somebody claims one", in the present tense and undated, which is a claim about `rules/gates/cra-scope.yaml` that this file cannot keep true (independent check, 2026-08-05). It held when measured on 2026-08-05 - `in-the-course-of-a-commercial-activity` carried `closes_gate_when: "false"` and the two free-and-open-source exemption limbs carried `"true"`, so a declaration is what closes that gate - and the description now states instead that no answer in this block claims an exemption, which is a fact about this file rather than about another. (ii) "EVERY FIELD IN THIS BLOCK DESCRIBES THE THING SUPPLIED" was false of two of the thirteen: `monetisation.not_for_profit_organisation` asks about the developing organisation's articles, as its own description says in terms, and `monetisation.only_between_microenterprises` asks about the counterparties to the transactions. All thirteen do take the product being scanned as their subject, which is the distinction the contributor carve-out needs, and the clause now says that. (iii) "THE PROFILE HAS NO FREE-TEXT FIELD ANYWHERE" WAS FALSE AND STOOD IN FOUR `$comment`s - at `licence.free_and_open_source`, `monetisation.by_the_manufacturer`, `monetisation.fee_recovers_operating_costs_only` and `monetisation.not_for_profit_organisation`. Measured on 2026-08-05, four fields elsewhere in this profile take arbitrary strings with neither an `enum` nor a `pattern` on them: `stacks[]`, `features.llm.providers[]`, `features.payments.provider` and `features.analytics_ads[]`. What is true, and what all four of those arguments actually rest on, is that `supply` has no free-text field - twelve booleans and one identifier confined to a published vocabulary - and that `additionalProperties: false` is set at every object level, measured the same day at 10 occurrences with no object-shaped subschema omitting the keyword. All four sentences now say that instead. It decides which carve-outs are even available: the two CRA routes out this block carries answers for - recital 18's route for software that its manufacturer does not monetise, and its route for a component intended for integration by other manufacturers - are open to free and open-source software and to nothing else, and it settles neither on its own, each being cumulative with `monetisation` below. TWO THINGS THAT COUNT ARE NOT AMONG THOSE ROUTES AND THIS FIELD DOES NOT GATE THEM. Recital 18 carries a third free-and-open-source proposition, on development by a not-for-profit organisation, which is answered at `monetisation.not_for_profit_organisation` and is not counted as a route out here because recital 18 puts it on the DEVELOPMENT side while Art. 3(22) makes the SUPPLY the thing that must be commercial. It does not make the converse true either: that a product is NOT free and open-source does not by itself make its supply commercial.

free_and_open_source.description: Is the product released under a free and open-source licence - COUNTING EVERYTHING SUPPLIED TOGETHER AS ONE RELEASE, THIRD-PARTY PARTS INCLUDED - with the source openly shared, AND a licence that gives everyone the right to make it freely accessible, usable, modifiable and redistributable? BOTH HALVES ARE REQUIRED AND THEY ARE REQUIRED OF THE WHOLE RELEASE: source you can read but not redistribute is `false`, and so is a release with any part under terms that are not free and open-source - a bundled proprietary font, a commercial driver, a licensed runtime, model weights on restricted terms. THAT YOUR OWN LICENCE IS MIT DOES NOT SETTLE IT. Copyleft and attribution conditions do not stop a licence being free and open-source, so GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0 and Apache-2.0 all answer `true` (that answer rule is the AI Act's own sentence - recital 102: "The licence should be considered to be free and open-source also when it allows users to run, copy, distribute, study, change and improve software and data, including models under the condition that the original provider of the model is credited, the identical or comparable terms of distribution are respected" - and it is THIS BLOCK'S READING that CRA Art. 3(48) reaches the same result, because a copyleft licence still provides for all rights to make the software freely accessible, usable, modifiable and redistributable; that second step is the one to disagree with rather than inherit, and the CRA has no sentence of its own like the AI Act's). WHAT ONE RELEASE MEANS. A container image, a desktop bundle, an installer and a vendored dependency tree are each one release, and code you redistribute unchanged is part of what the recipient receives on your terms, so it counts. Third-party parts that are themselves free and open-source do not make the answer `false`, because they meet the test on their own; an ordinary `node_modules` of permissive and copyleft dependencies is still `true`. (That the release rather than the first-party code is the unit is this block's reading; neither instrument says which parts of a bundle to count.) WHICH THING YOU ARE ANSWERING FOR. Where a repository ships a free core beside a paid edition under a separate licence, those are two releases: answer for the one being scanned, not for the repository. The question is how the product is RELEASED, not what a file in the tree says: a `license` field reading `MIT` in a scaffold-generated manifest with no licence text behind it is not an answer. A `true` settles ONE element of each CRA carve-out and nothing on its own - qualifying as free and open-source software changes nothing until the monetisation answer is given too. A `false` closes those routes and says nothing about whether the supply is commercial. THE PROFILE RECORDS ONLY THE YES OR NO: it has no field for which part of a release failed, and a `false` does not name it.
free_and_open_source.$comment: CRA Art. 3(48) defines free and open-source software as "software the source code of which is openly shared and which is made available under a free and open-source licence which provides for all rights to make it freely accessible, usable, modifiable and redistributable". That is where the two cumulative elements come from. THE AI ACT ASKS A CLOSE QUESTION AND ART. 2(12) IS NOT WHERE ITS CONTENT IS. Art. 2(12) reads in full: "This Regulation does not apply to AI systems released under free and open-source licences, unless they are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems or as an AI system that falls under Article 5 or 50." That provision defines nothing, and citing it alone for the definition was a gap the independent check of 2026-08-05 found. Recital 102 supplies the content - "Software and data, including models, released under a free and open-source licence that allows them to be openly shared and where users can freely access, use, modify and redistribute them or modified versions thereof" - and adds a sentence with no CRA counterpart: "The licence should be considered to be free and open-source also when it allows users to run, copy, distribute, study, change and improve software and data, including models under the condition that the original provider of the model is credited, the identical or comparable terms of distribution are respected." THE AI ACT ALSO STATES A FREE-AND-OPEN-SOURCE LICENCE TEST IN ITS ENACTING TERMS, TWICE, AND THIS BOOLEAN DOES NOT CARRY IT - added 2026-08-05, when the same sweep that found Art. 25(4) missing from this block measured the Regulation for free-and-open-source provisions it had never cited. Art. 53(2) begins "The obligations set out in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b), shall not apply to providers of AI models that are released under a free and open-source licence" and Art. 54(6) begins "The obligation set out in this Article shall not apply to providers of general-purpose AI models that are released under a free and open-source licence"; both then state the test in the same words - "a free and open-source licence that allows for the access, usage, modification, and distribution of the model, and whose parameters, including the weights, the information on the model architecture, and the information on model usage, are made publicly available" - and both take it away again for systemic risk, Art. 53(2) with "This exception shall not apply to general-purpose AI models with systemic risks" and Art. 54(6) with "unless the general-purpose AI models present systemic risks". THAT TEST HAS A THIRD ELEMENT THIS FIELD DOES NOT ASK: publicly available parameters. A `true` here answers CRA Art. 3(48)'s two elements and recital 102's account of what such a licence allows; it does not answer Arts. 53(2) or 54(6), which are addressed to providers of models rather than to AI systems and which recital 104 governs separately. No field in this block asks about parameters and adding one would be a granularity decision, so what is recorded here is the gap and not a fix for it. SO THE COPYLEFT ANSWER RULE IS THE AI ACT'S AND THE CRA HAS NO SENTENCE LIKE IT, which matters because this one field serves both instruments (independent check, 2026-08-05). A CRA-only reader takes the answer from Art. 3(48) instead and reaches the same place by a different route: a copyleft licence still provides for all rights to make the software freely accessible, usable, modifiable and redistributable, so it satisfies Art. 3(48). That last step is THIS BLOCK'S READING of Art. 3(48) and not a CRA sentence, and it is labelled so a reader can disagree with it rather than inherit it silently from the other instrument. THE UNIT THE ANSWER IS GIVEN FOR, AND TWO WITHDRAWN FORMULATIONS OF IT. The unit was originally stated as "The product", singular, where a repository ships several things; that phrasing is kept here because the two formulations below were attempts to sharpen it. (a) The earlier wording "the component that matters" is withdrawn as undefined (independent check, 2026-08-05): it collided with the instruction to answer for the thing that is supplied, and two honest readers answered a bundled product differently. (b) The earlier form of the rule set the unit as "any part of that thing which a claimed exemption would have to cover", and that is withdrawn because it is not knowable when the field is filled in, the field being filled in before any exemption is claimed (independent check, 2026-08-05). The unit is now what is supplied together as one release, which is knowable then, and a freely licensed wrapper supplied together with model weights on restricted terms is therefore `false`. Recital 103's first sentence sets the AI Act's own unit and points the same way: "Free and open-source AI components covers the software and data, including models and general-purpose AI models, tools, services or processes of an AI system." CORRECTED 2026-08-05, ON THE RECITAL 102 QUOTATION ABOVE. Its run-up used to stand outside the quotation marks as "software and data", which are the Official Journal's own words with ", including models," dropped at the join and no ellipsis marking the drop. The quotation now starts at the recital's own "Software and data, including models, released under". This is the mirror image of the correction recorded at `supply`'s `$comment` as (viii), where the Journal's words ran on AFTER a closing quote mark and only that direction was fixed; and the dropped words are not inert here, "including models" being the link this `$comment` draws its argument across when it says Arts. 53(2) and 54(6) are addressed to providers of models (independent check, 2026-08-05). (c1) WHERE THE RELEASE-UNIT RULE STANDS IN THE DESCRIPTION, MOVED 2026-08-05. It sat about 40% of the way in, behind an opening sentence entirely about the licence, and an independent check on that date found this the one field in the block where the field name still decides the answer: a developer shipping a container image with one proprietary component reads the name and the first two sentences, sees that their own licence is MIT and that both halves of the licence test are met, and answers `true` where the answer is `false`. That is the unsafe direction on both instruments, this field's `true` being a cumulative element of every carve-out here. The rule is now inside the opening question. (c) THIRD-PARTY COMPONENTS INSIDE A RELEASE were unaddressed until 2026-08-05, when an independent check found that two honest readers answered the same container image differently - read literally the rule made almost every shipped artefact `false`, and read as its sole worked example suggested it covered only first-party parts. The description now says third-party parts count and that free and open-source ones do not make the answer `false`. That is this block's reading and not a sentence in either instrument.
